title: Sticky segment allocation and granular eviction policy for paged KV cache
creator: Aisha Malhotra
description: Introduce a sticky segment allocation strategy and a fine-grained eviction/scoring policy for the paged KV cache to reduce fragmentation, lower decode tail latency, and improve overall token cost. This ticket covers algorithm design, prototype on a single-runtime instance, microbenchmarks, integration with kernel selection heuristics, and a staged rollout with feature flags. The approach focuses on minimizing disruptive evictions for hot prefixes while keeping background compaction CPU bounded.
acceptance_criteria: Total KV eviction rate reduced by >=20% on representative workload (chat-heavy, mid-sequence lengths)
P99 decode latency improves by >=10ms in baseline production trace or stays within SLO while token cost decreases
Fragmentation metric (free segments per shard) reduced by >=25% after 24h of mixed traffic
Prototype gated behind runtime feature flag and passes automated correctness tests for concurrent prefill + decode
No >5% increase in CPU usage on compactor host under normal steady state (benchmarked)
tasks: Design sticky segment allocator and eviction scoring RFC
Implement allocation bookkeeping and per-segment sticky counters
Add eviction scorer that combines recency, decode-priority, segment-utilization, and model-variant weighting
Integrate hints from prefill scheduler to mark segments as prefetch-protected for short windows
Implement background compaction with rate limiter and low-priority scheduling
Add unit and integration tests for concurrent access patterns
Run microbenchmarks and end-to-end load tests against perf harness
Create GitHub PR and request design/pm reviews
Rollout behind feature flag and monitor metrics; prepare rollback plan

implementation_notes: Allocation: prefer allocating new segments from a 'sticky pool' when a session issues repeated prefill requests; increment sticky_count per allocation and decay with exponential backoff
Eviction scoring: score = w1*recency_rank + w2*sticky_boost + w3*decode_priority - w4*utilization_penalty; weights tunable via feature flag
Fragmentation repair: background compactor merges adjacent free segments when contiguous free bytes exceed threshold; compactor runs bounded by a token-bucket rate limiter tied to CPU headroom
Reuse: prefer reassigning reclaimed segments to the same model-shard for short-sticky window to exploit temporal locality
Kernel selection interplay: allocator annotates segments with quantization_hint and expected sequence_length distribution so kernel selector can prebind preferred kernel variant
Prefill scheduler hints: when prefill schedules a long prefix, it emits a 'hold' hint to allocator to delay eviction for that segment for N seconds
Concurrency: use optimistic concurrency for per-segment metadata and fall back to lightweight per-shard locks during compaction to avoid stalls on hot paths
Telemetry: emit per-shard eviction_reason, sticky_count, compaction_cycles, and hold_hint_misses for troubleshooting
Safety: forced eviction (out-of-memory) bypasses sticky boost but increments a forced_eviction counter; surfaced in logs and console
